standard_prerequisites.name: Tor against a quotient by a power of an ideal is an essentially constant pro-zero system
standard_prerequisites.use: Makes the obstruction to commuting tensor products with the limit vanish.

standard_prerequisites.name: Mittag-Leffler style lemma identifying the limit of a cokernel with the cokernel of the limits
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Homology, Lemma \ref{homology-lemma-apply-Mittag-Leffler-again}, cited at proof lines 6500 and 6519
standard_prerequisites.use: Produces the isomorphism between the tensor product with the limit and the limit of the tensor products, and the injectivity of the limit of the maps.

standard_prerequisites.name: Flatness is detected by injectivity of tensoring with injective maps of modules
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Algebra, Lemma \ref{algebra-lemma-flat}, cited at proof lines 6508-6509
standard_prerequisites.use: Turns the second part of the proof into a criterion for flatness of the limit module.

core_obligations: Choose a finite free resolution of a finite module and write down the resulting complex for each M_n (proof lines 6487-6494).
Identify the degree one homology with Tor against the base ring using flatness of M_n over the quotient, and note that the system is essentially constant with value zero (proof lines 6495-6499).
Apply the Mittag-Leffler lemma to identify the limit of the tensor products with the tensor product with the limit (proof lines 6500-6505).
Reduce flatness to injectivity on injective maps of finite modules and rewrite the kernel as the kernel of the limit of the maps (proof lines 6506-6512).
Use the exact Tor sequences and the essentially constant vanishing to conclude that the limit of the maps is injective, hence that the limit module is flat (proof lines 6513-6524).
proof_roadmap: Compute the tensor product with a finite module through a free resolution (proof lines 6487-6505).
Reduce flatness to injectivity on finite modules (proof lines 6506-6512).
Conclude injectivity from the vanishing Tor systems (proof lines 6513-6524).
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves that the inverse limit of a surjective system of modules flat over the successive quotients by powers of an ideal is flat over the ring, and that tensoring with any finite module commutes with the limit. The proof first computes the tensor product with a finite module using a finite free resolution: the degree one homology of the resulting complex is a Tor group that is essentially constant with value zero by an earlier vanishing result, so a Mittag-Leffler lemma identifies the limit of the tensor products with the cokernel computed from the limit module. Flatness is then checked on injective maps of finite modules, where the same essentially-constant Tor systems and the Mittag-Leffler lemma show that the limit of the maps stays injective.
